name: GamePark GP32
description: A South Korean handheld from GamePark, released in 2001. It used an ARM9 processor, a 320 × 240 colour screen and standard SmartMedia cards instead of proprietary cartridges. Few commercial games came out, but it became a favourite of homebrew developers and emulator authors.
curiosities: GamePark gave away its development tools, and the community wrote far more software for it than was ever sold commercially.
It shipped in three screen versions: no light (NLU), frontlit (FLU) and backlit (BLU).
Many units could be overclocked well beyond the stock 133 MHz to run emulators faster.
Some of GamePark's staff left to form GamePark Holdings, which made its successor, the GP2X.
